title: GCP — GS1 Company Prefix
objectives: Understand GCP via a real-life analogy
Parse a GCP out of a GTIN / GLN / SSCC
Choose the right GCP length for a company's needs
Handle GCP updates when GS1 restructures

sections.markdown:
**Think of a GCP as your company's telephone area code — assigned by GS1.**

Every GS1 identifier (GTIN, GLN, SSCC, GRAI, GIAI, ...) STARTS with a **GS1 Company Prefix** — a variable-length block of digits GS1 assigns to your company. Everything after the GCP is yours to allocate.

- **Variable length** — from 4 digits to 12 digits. Shorter = you can register with more products; longer = smaller company with fewer products to identify.
- **Prefix determines country of ISSUE**, not manufacture — GS1 India assigns `890xxx`; GS1 US assigns various ranges.
- **Everything after the GCP is your item reference** — 500 g pack vs 1 kg pack vs the 12-count case.
- **Parsing a GTIN back into GCP + item reference** requires a lookup — GCP length isn't encoded in the number itself.

**Why every serious retail integration must resolve GCPs correctly:** partner catalogs join on GCP → brand owner. Get the parse wrong (assume 6-digit GCP when it's actually 8) and you attribute products to the wrong company. GS1 provides the **GS1 GEPIR** service — global directory that maps GCP → company. Big apps cache GEPIR lookups locally.

**GCP (GS1 Company Prefix)** is the variable-length numeric prefix GS1 issues to a company that identifies them uniquely worldwide. It sits at the start of every GS1 key issued by that company (GTIN, GLN, SSCC, GRAI, GIAI, GDTI, GSIN, GSRN). Length varies (typically 6-10 digits). Combined with an item reference + check digit forms a full GS1 key.
## GCP prefix highlights (country of ISSUE)

## Parsing GCP from a GTIN

GCP length isn't encoded in the barcode — you need GS1's **GCP length table** (published as CSV). Common lengths for the 890 range: 7 digits (`890xxxx`) is typical, but some GS1 India allocations are 6-, 8-, or 10-digit.
## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Assuming fixed GCP length.** 'It's 7 digits' — no, it varies per company. Always look up in the current GCP-length CSV.
**Mistake 2: Cache never invalidated.** The GCP length table + GEPIR data change over time. Sync monthly.
**Mistake 3: Attribute product to prefix's country of ISSUE.** 890 = registered via GS1 India ≠ manufactured in India. Don't display 'Made in India' from GCP alone.
**Mistake 4: Ignoring ISBN / ISSN GCPs.** 978/979 books + 977 serials look like normal GTINs but have their own catalog systems.
**Mistake 5: Confusing GCP with GS1 Prefix.** GS1 Prefix is the FIRST 3 digits (identifies the Member Organization); GCP is the full company prefix (which INCLUDES the GS1 Prefix).
**Mistake 6: Ignoring restricted-circulation prefixes.** 02 + some 04-09 prefixes are in-store; GCP doesn't apply.
**Mistake 7: Storing without leading zeros.** GCPs starting with `0` corrupt when stored as int.
**Mistake 8: Trusting user-typed GCP.** Users guess; always validate against the authoritative GEPIR service or your synced snapshot.
## Best practices
**1. Sync GCP length table monthly.**
**2. Cache GEPIR lookups** with TTL.
**3. Store GCP as TEXT** — never int.
**4. Attribute country of registration** (not manufacture).
**5. Detect restricted prefixes** + branch handling.
**6. Log unknown-prefix products** for catalog cleanup.
**7. Handle ISBN / ISSN specially** — different lookup services.
**8. Never let users edit a product's GCP field manually** — derived from GTIN.

**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Sync GCP length CSV from GS1 + refresh Hive cache.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — GEPIR lookup with retry + cache TTL.

## Interview Q&A

**Q1: How do you parse a GTIN into GCP + item reference?**

**A:** GTIN itself doesn't encode where the GCP ends. You need the **GS1 GCP length table** (published as CSV by GS1). For a GTIN-14 (padded), strip the leading indicator digit, then look up the longest matching prefix in the table to find the length. That's your GCP; everything after (except the check digit) is the item reference. **Cache the table locally**; refresh monthly. **Common bug:** hardcoding '7 digits' — works for many companies but fails for the ones with shorter or longer prefixes. **Interview signal:** knowing the length table exists AT ALL.

**Q2: What's the GS1 Prefix vs GCP?**

**A:** **GS1 Prefix** — the FIRST 2-3 digits of the GCP, identifies the GS1 Member Organization that issued it. Example: `890` = GS1 India. **GCP** — the full company prefix INCLUDING those first digits. Example: `8901234` (7-digit GCP for an Indian company). **Every GCP includes a GS1 Prefix.** The GS1 Prefix tells you 'which MO issued this,' not the brand owner. The GCP identifies the brand owner. Both matter for compliance + attribution. Interviewer bonus: knowing that `978/979` (bookland) + `977` (serials) are GS1 Prefixes reserved for ISBN + ISSN.

**Q3: Why can't you infer country-of-manufacture from GCP?**

**A:** GS1 Prefix tells you where the GCP was ISSUED — which Member Organization the company registered with — NOT where the product was made. An Indian brand may have used GS1 US to register their US-facing SKUs; a Chinese factory may make products for a French brand whose GCP is `300xxx`. **Displaying 'Made in India' from `890` prefix = misleading + legally risky.** Real country-of-origin is a separate data attribute + regulated by customs / packaging laws. **Interview signal:** distinguishing 'registered' from 'manufactured' + 'sold.'

**Q4: How does GEPIR fit in + how would you use it?**

**A:** **GEPIR (Global Electronic Party Information Registry)** is GS1's global directory that maps GCP → brand owner + address + contact. Free HTTP service (rate-limited). **Use:** on ingesting an unfamiliar GTIN, resolve its GCP + query GEPIR to identify the brand owner + populate catalog metadata. **Cache aggressively** — GEPIR data changes slowly; TTL of days is safe. **Alternative:** GS1's Verified by GS1 API + GS1 Registry — more authoritative, covers GTIN-level lookups (not just GCP). **For India-specific data**, GS1 India also maintains a directory. **Interview senior signal:** integrating GEPIR into your data-quality pipeline.

**Q5: What happens when GS1 restructures / expands a GCP length?**

**A:** GS1 occasionally publishes new GCP-length rules: some prefixes get subdivided (a `6-digit` prefix range becomes a mix of `7-digit` and `8-digit` prefixes as GS1 allocates deeper into it). **Impact on your app:** the same GTIN parsed with the old table might attribute to a different company under the new table. **Handle:** monthly sync of the length table; re-attribute historic products on major changes; log discrepancies for manual review. **Rare but painful** — a catalog that misattributes 5000 products because of a stale length table causes real business impact. Interviewer bonus: knowing the length table CAN change.

**Q6: How would you architect GCP handling in a Flutter e-commerce app?**

**A:** **(1)** Bundle a starter GCP-length CSV in the app; sync monthly to refresh. **(2)** On product ingest, extract GCP via the table + store both `gtin14` + `gcp` on the row. **(3)** Resolve brand-owner via GEPIR lookup + cache. **(4)** UI shows 'Brand: X Ltd (verified)' when GEPIR confirms; 'Unknown brand' when not. **(5)** Restricted-circulation prefixes (`2xx`, `04-09`) flagged + branch handling. **(6)** On catalog import, log unknown-brand ingestion for manual triage. **(7)** Analytics: track resolution rates + latency; a drop suggests stale table.

## Real-world usage

- **E-commerce catalogs** — resolve brand owner per GTIN.
- **Compliance apps** — verify GCP registration for regulated categories.
- **Retail POS** — quick brand attribution.
- **Pharma track-and-trace** — GCP embedded in every SGTIN.
- **NOT for** — end-user display of country of manufacture.

## Advanced notes

- **GS1 GCP length table** — CSV downloadable from GS1 sites; format `prefix,length`.
- **GEPIR** — global directory service; free tier + paid enterprise.
- **Verified by GS1** — modern API for authoritative GTIN + brand + attributes.
- **Restricted-circulation prefixes** (in-store) — no GCP applies.
- **GS1 India** — 890 range; also handles education + training + compliance.
- **VOICE prefixes** — 977/978/979 for ISSN + ISBN.
- **GS1 Prefix changes** — infrequent but real; monitor GS1 announcements.
- **GCP hijacking** — pirate use of another company's GCP; legal action + GS1 dispute process.
- **Small-brand GCPs** — GS1 India offers licenses for start-ups; length varies.
- **App size** — a full GCP length table is ~200 KB CSV; sync incrementally.
- **Attribution UI** — pair GCP-derived brand name with a 'source: GEPIR' badge for transparency.
